questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Domain Name System (DNS)?
questions.option_b: B. Map hostnames to IP addresses
questions.explanation: DNS is primarily used to translate human-readable hostnames into IP addresses.

questions.question: Why are symbolic hostnames preferred over numeric IP addresses?
questions.option_b: B. They are easier for computers to process
questions.option_c: C. They are easier for humans to remember
questions.explanation: Hostnames are easier for humans to remember compared to numeric IP addresses.

questions.question: Which DNS record type maps a hostname to an IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: An A record maps a hostname to a 32-bit IPv4 address.

questions.question: Which DNS record type is used for IPv6 address mapping?
questions.explanation: AAAA records map hostnames to 128-bit IPv6 addresses.

questions.question: What does an MX record specify?
questions.option_a: A. Alias name of a host
questions.explanation: MX records identify mail servers responsible for handling email for a domain.

questions.question: Which DNS record type is commonly used for reverse DNS lookups?
questions.explanation: PTR records map IP addresses back to hostnames.

questions.question: What does DNS caching primarily improve?
questions.explanation: Caching reduces repeated lookups and improves DNS response times.

questions.question: What does TTL stand for in DNS?
questions.explanation: TTL defines how long a DNS record may remain cached.

questions.question: Which top-level domain is associated with educational institutions?
questions.explanation: The .edu domain is reserved for educational institutions.

questions.question: Which organization assigns unique domain suffixes?
questions.explanation: IANA manages Internet Assigned Numbers and domain assignments.

questions.question: What is iterative query resolution in DNS?
questions.option_b: B. Traversing DNS hierarchy step by step
questions.explanation: Iterative resolution involves querying multiple DNS servers stepwise to resolve a name.

questions.question: Why are root DNS servers replicated worldwide?
questions.option_c: C. To improve availability and scalability
questions.explanation: Replication distributes load and improves fault tolerance.

questions.question: What transport protocol is typically used by DNS queries?
questions.explanation: DNS commonly uses UDP for fast query-response communication.

questions.question: What is the role of the resolver in DNS?
questions.option_c: C. Communicate with DNS servers on behalf of applications
questions.explanation: Resolvers are library functions used by applications to query DNS servers.

questions.question: Which function maps a hostname to an IP address?
questions.explanation: gethostbyname() resolves hostnames into IP addresses.

questions.question: Which function performs reverse DNS lookups?
questions.explanation: gethostbyaddr() maps IP addresses to hostnames.

questions.question: Which structure is returned by gethostbyname()?
questions.explanation: gethostbyname() returns a pointer to a hostent structure.

questions.question: What does the h_name field in hostent represent?
questions.explanation: h_name stores the official canonical hostname.

questions.question: What does h_aliases contain?
questions.option_c: C. Alias names for the host
questions.explanation: h_aliases stores alternative names associated with the host.

questions.question: Which constant indicates IPv4 addresses in hostent?
questions.explanation: AF_INET identifies IPv4 address family.

questions.question: What does AF_INET6 represent?
questions.explanation: AF_INET6 identifies IPv6 address family.

questions.question: What happens if gethostbyname() fails?
questions.option_b: B. NULL is returned and h_errno is set
questions.explanation: On failure, gethostbyname() returns NULL and sets h_errno.

questions.question: Which error constant indicates a temporary DNS failure?
questions.explanation: TRY_AGAIN indicates a temporary and recoverable failure.

questions.question: What is the purpose of hstrerror()?
questions.option_c: C. Translate h_errno into readable text
questions.explanation: hstrerror() converts resolver error codes into human-readable messages.

questions.question: Why is DNS considered a distributed database?
questions.option_a: A. All records exist in one server
questions.option_b: B. Data is spread across many coordinated servers
questions.option_c: C. It stores only local records
questions.explanation: DNS information is distributed among multiple hierarchical servers.

questions.question: Which statement about authoritative DNS records is correct?
questions.option_a: A. They are always cached records
questions.option_b: B. They come from the server responsible for the domain
questions.option_c: C. They are generated by clients
questions.explanation: Authoritative records originate from servers managing the domain.

questions.question: What is the benefit of temporal locality in DNS caching?
questions.option_a: A. Users repeatedly access similar domain names
questions.explanation: Users often access the same domains repeatedly, making caching effective.

questions.question: Which field of hostent contains IP addresses?
questions.explanation: h_addr_list stores one or more IP addresses associated with the host.

questions.question: What does gethostbyname2() add compared to gethostbyname()?
questions.explanation: gethostbyname2() supports both IPv4 and IPv6 lookups.

questions.question: Which argument specifies address family in gethostbyname2()?
questions.explanation: The family parameter specifies AF_INET or AF_INET6.

questions.question: What does uname() primarily provide?
questions.explanation: uname() provides OS and node-related system information.

questions.question: Which field in utsname stores the hostname of the machine?
questions.explanation: nodename stores the current machine's hostname.

questions.question: What does gethostname() return?
questions.explanation: gethostname() retrieves the current host's name.

questions.question: What information does getservbyname() return?
questions.option_c: C. Service information including port number
questions.explanation: getservbyname() returns service details such as protocol and port.

questions.question: Why would getservbyname("ftp", "udp") fail?
questions.option_d: D. UDP does not support ports
questions.explanation: FTP is defined to operate over TCP, not UDP.

questions.question: What does getservbyport() perform?
questions.option_a: A. Maps port numbers to services
questions.option_b: B. Maps hostnames to MAC addresses
questions.explanation: getservbyport() identifies services associated with a given port.

questions.question: Why is htons() used with getservbyport()?
questions.option_a: A. To convert port numbers to network byte order
questions.explanation: Ports must be represented in network byte order.

questions.question: A resolver repeatedly contacts the root server for common domains despite caching being enabled. Which issue is MOST likely?
questions.option_a: A. TTL values expire too quickly
questions.explanation: Very short TTL values reduce cache usefulness and force repeated queries.

questions.question: A company wants both www.example.com and ftp.example.com to point to the same host. Which DNS record is MOST suitable?
questions.explanation: CNAME records create aliases pointing to another canonical hostname.

questions.question: A network application must support IPv6-only systems. Which resolver function is MOST appropriate?
questions.explanation: gethostbyname2() explicitly supports IPv6 via AF_INET6.

questions.question: Why are cached DNS responses considered non-authoritative?
questions.explanation: Cached records may become stale over time and are not directly managed by authoritative servers.

questions.question: An application calls gethostbyaddr() using an IPv6 address but passes AF_INET. What is the likely outcome?
questions.explanation: Incorrect address family usage causes lookup failure.

questions.question: Which DNS optimization directly reduces root server load?
questions.explanation: Caching prevents repeated requests from reaching root servers.

questions.question: A DNS server knows how to reach root servers but not a target domain directly. What happens next?
questions.explanation: The server iteratively queries higher-level servers to locate the authoritative server.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of binary IP addresses over symbolic names?
questions.option_a: A. Easier for humans to memorize
questions.option_b: B. Require less computation and memory
questions.explanation: Binary IP addresses are compact and computationally efficient.

questions.question: What is multihoming in networking?
questions.option_a: A. A host having multiple IP addresses
questions.option_b: B. A router having one interface
questions.explanation: Multihoming allows a host to use multiple network interfaces or addresses.

questions.question: Which field of hostent indicates address size?
questions.explanation: h_length specifies the size of the address in bytes.

questions.question: Why might DNS overuse root servers without caching?
questions.option_a: A. Each lookup would require root-level queries
questions.explanation: Without caching, every lookup would begin from root servers, causing excessive load.

questions.question: What does the Class field in a DNS resource record commonly contain for Internet data?
questions.explanation: IN represents the Internet class in DNS records.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes an FQDN?
questions.option_c: C. A fully qualified domain name
questions.explanation: FQDN stands for Fully Qualified Domain Name.

questions.question: Why are domain names considered case-insensitive?
questions.option_b: B. EDU and edu are treated identically
questions.explanation: DNS does not distinguish between uppercase and lowercase letters.

questions.question: Which resolver function would MOST likely be used internally after uname() in determining local IP addresses?
questions.explanation: The nodename obtained from uname() is resolved using gethostbyname().

questions.question: A system administrator wants to identify the hostname associated with IP 192.168.1.20. Which DNS record is queried?
questions.explanation: PTR records support reverse DNS lookups from IP addresses to hostnames.

questions.question: Which statement about DNS hierarchy is TRUE?
questions.option_a: A. Every DNS server stores all Internet records
questions.option_b: B. Root servers directly store every hostname
questions.option_c: C. Authority is distributed among hierarchical servers
questions.option_d: D. DNS hierarchy exists only for IPv4
questions.explanation: DNS distributes authority among hierarchical domain servers.

questions.question: What would MOST likely happen if h_addr_list contains multiple entries?
questions.option_a: A. The host has multiple associated IP addresses
questions.explanation: Multiple entries indicate multiple IP addresses for the host.

questions.question: Why is DNS especially important for IPv6?
questions.option_b: B. IPv6 addresses are significantly longer
questions.option_d: D. IPv6 uses MAC addresses only
questions.explanation: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits long and difficult for humans to remember.

questions.question: Which field in the servent structure is MOST important for socket programming?
questions.explanation: s_port contains the network service port number.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the resolver configuration file shown in the architecture diagram?
questions.option_b: B. Specify how resolvers communicate with DNS servers
questions.explanation: Resolver configuration files define DNS server information used by applications.

questions.question: A developer uses gethostbyname() for an IPv6-only host and receives failures. What is the BEST fix?
questions.explanation: gethostbyname() is IPv4-oriented, while gethostbyname2() supports IPv6.

questions.question: What is the significance of the in-addr.arpa domain?
questions.option_b: B. It supports reverse IPv4 lookups
questions.option_d: D. It stores IPv6 AAAA records
questions.explanation: Reverse IPv4 DNS lookups use the in-addr.arpa domain.

questions.question: Which operation would MOST likely involve getservbyport()?
questions.option_a: A. Determining which service uses TCP port 21
questions.explanation: getservbyport() maps ports back to service names.

questions.question: Why are plausible alias records useful in DNS?
questions.option_b: B. They allow multiple service names for one host
questions.explanation: Aliases allow convenient naming for services hosted on the same system.

questions.question: A DNS response contains stale information because the hostname changed recently. Which DNS mechanism contributes MOST to this issue?
questions.explanation: Caching can temporarily retain outdated records until TTL expires.

questions.question: What is the relationship between applications and resolvers?
questions.option_a: A. Applications directly contact root servers
questions.option_b: B. Resolvers act as intermediary libraries for applications
questions.explanation: Applications use resolver libraries to perform DNS operations.

questions.question: Why is UDP preferred for most DNS operations?
questions.option_b: B. It has lower overhead and faster communication
questions.explanation: UDP provides lightweight communication suitable for quick DNS queries.

questions.question: A DNS administrator notices that local domain queries are significantly faster than remote ones. Which DNS principle BEST explains this?
questions.explanation: DNS caching and locality of reference improve access speed for frequently used local domains.
